## Spherical-polar metric and sources (`spherical-polar`) {#sec-ch03-sphpolar}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274 (chengcli/snapy, code_pin.yml)
sources: src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp, src/coord/spherical_polar.hpp, src/coord/coordinate.hpp, tests/test_coordinate.cpp
status: draft
-->

On a spherical-polar grid $(x_1, x_2, x_3) = (r, \theta, \varphi)$ every face area and volume is the exact integral of
the metric over the cell, so the discrete divergence of a uniform field is exact, and the cell centres are volume
centroids, so a stored cell value sits where a cell average of a linear field equals the point value. Because the
basis vectors turn from cell to cell, the momentum equations carry geometric source terms. The radial one can be
written so that the pressure force reduces to the plain face difference of the Riemann solver's face pressure,
which the well-balanced reconstruction of @sec-ch05 balances against gravity.

Local symbols: $r_\pm = x_{1,i\pm1/2}$ and $\theta_\pm = x_{2,j\pm1/2}$, the faces of one cell;
$\Delta\theta = \theta_+ - \theta_-$ and $\Delta\varphi$ the cell's angular widths [rad]; $x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i} = \tfrac12(r_- + r_+)$
the radial midpoint of the cell [m]; $\mathsf T = \rho\mathbf v\mathbf v + p\mathsf I$ the momentum flux tensor
[$\mathrm{Pa}$], with physical components $T_{ab}$;
$f^{(a)}_{i\pm1/2}$ the $x_1$ face flux of the momentum component $m_a$ (`flux1[IVY]`, `flux1[IVZ]`) [$\mathrm{kg\,m^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$]; $p_{i\pm1/2}$ the face pressure returned by the Riemann solver
[$\mathrm{Pa}$].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** The exact $r^2\sin\theta$ measures of a spherical-polar cell (@eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric), volume
centroids for the cell centres, and the curvature sources of the momentum equations.

**Data.** In: global faces in $r$[^rg-8f3539a20049] [m], $\theta$[^rg-f8c6079838f7], $\varphi$[^rg-d44d77aee75f] [rad]. Out: areas [m$^2$], volumes [m$^3$], centres
`x1v`, `x2v`, source coefficients.

**Placement.** Metric at setup (`reset`); sources in every stage.

**Activation.** YAML `geometry.type: spherical-polar`; off by default. Requires $x_2$ inside $[0,\pi]$.

**Guarantee / limits.** Metric exact; source terms second order. Centres are volume centroids in $r$ and $\theta$,
except that with a single $x_2$ cell `x2v` is the midpoint; $x_{3,k}$ is always the midpoint.

**Evidence.** `test_coordinate`, `test_x1_centroid_rest_python`; checks `[C4]`, `[C5]`; the ctest entries were
not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).
:::

The scheme is on when `geometry.type` is `spherical-polar`. Its $x_1$ pressure source has a second form under
`SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` (@sec-ch05 owns that form); the curved-face corrections of @sec-ch04 read the radial face
moments of @sec-ch03-facemoments. The coefficient names `coord_src1_i` to `coord_src3_j` follow the code.

### Derivation

The volume element and the area elements of the three face families are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{d}V &= r^2\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta\,\mathrm{d}\varphi, \\
\mathrm{d}A_1 &= r^2\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta\,\mathrm{d}\varphi \quad\text{on } r = r_\pm, \\
\mathrm{d}A_2 &= r\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\varphi \quad\text{on } \theta = \theta_\pm, \\
\mathrm{d}A_3 &= r\,\mathrm{d}r\,\mathrm{d}\theta \quad\text{on } \varphi = \varphi_\pm.
\end{aligned}
$$

The integrals over one cell separate into the one-dimensional factors

$$
\int_{r_-}^{r_+} r\,\mathrm{d}r = \tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right), \qquad
\int_{r_-}^{r_+} r^2\,\mathrm{d}r = \tfrac13\left(r_+^3 - r_-^3\right), \qquad
\int_{\theta_-}^{\theta_+} \sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+,
$$

and the $\varphi$ integral gives $\Delta\varphi$. Multiplying the factors of each element gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_{i\pm1/2} &= r_\pm^2\,\lvert\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+\rvert\,\Delta\varphi, \\
A_{j\pm1/2} &= \tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right)\lvert\sin\theta_\pm\rvert\,\Delta\varphi, \\
A_{k\pm1/2} &= \tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right)\Delta\theta, \\
V_i &= \tfrac13\left(r_+^3 - r_-^3\right)\lvert\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+\rvert\,\Delta\varphi.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric}

With the definitions in @sec-appa-index, $V_i = \varpi_{jk}V^{(1)}_i$ with $V^{(1)}_i = \tfrac13(r_+^3-r_-^3)$ and the solid
angle $\varpi_{jk} = \lvert\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+\rvert\Delta\varphi$. @eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric is
`face_area1` to `face_area3` and `cell_volume` ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::cell_volume >}}, {{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::face_area1 >}}, {{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::face_area2 >}}, {{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::face_area3 >}}).

The cell centres are the centroids of the measure along each axis:

$$
\begin{aligned}
x_{1,i} &= \frac{\int r^3\,\mathrm{d}r}{\int r^2\,\mathrm{d}r}
         = \frac34\,\frac{r_+^4 - r_-^4}{r_+^3 - r_-^3}, \\
x_{2,j} &= \frac{\int \theta\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta}{\int\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta}
         = \frac{(\sin\theta_+ - \theta_+\cos\theta_+) - (\sin\theta_- - \theta_-\cos\theta_-)}{\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids}

with the integrals over the cell's own interval and $x_{3,k}$ the midpoint. @eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids is
`radial_centers` and `polar_centers` ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp polar_centers >}}, {{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp radial_centers >}}); with a single $x_2$ cell the code sets `x2v`
to the midpoint instead ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::reset >}}).

The momentum equation is $\partial_t(\rho\mathbf v) + \nabla\cdot\mathsf T = 0$. Its physical components
$m_a = \rho v_a$ need the components of $\nabla\cdot\mathsf T$ in the turning basis
$(\hat{\mathbf e}_r, \hat{\mathbf e}_\theta, \hat{\mathbf e}_\varphi)$. For a symmetric $\mathsf T$ the radial and polar
components are

$$
\begin{aligned}
(\nabla\cdot\mathsf T)_r &= \frac{1}{r^2}\partial_r\left(r^2T_{rr}\right)
  + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\partial_\theta\left(\sin\theta\,T_{\theta r}\right)
  + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\partial_\varphi T_{\varphi r}
  - \frac{T_{\theta\theta} + T_{\varphi\varphi}}{r}, \\
(\nabla\cdot\mathsf T)_\theta &= \frac{1}{r^2}\partial_r\left(r^2T_{r\theta}\right)
  + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\partial_\theta\left(\sin\theta\,T_{\theta\theta}\right)
  + \frac{1}{r\sin\theta}\partial_\varphi T_{\varphi\theta}
  + \frac{T_{r\theta} - \cot\theta\,T_{\varphi\varphi}}{r}.
\end{aligned}
$$

In each row the first three terms are the divergence of the flux row in conservation form: the code's face-area
difference over the volume. The last term is the turning of the basis, and it moves to the right-hand side as a
source. With $\mathsf T = \rho\mathbf v\mathbf v + p\mathsf I$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_{\theta\theta} + T_{\varphi\varphi} &= \rho\left(v_2^2 + v_3^2\right) + 2p, \\
T_{r\theta} &= \rho v_1v_2, \qquad T_{\varphi\varphi} = \rho v_3^2 + p,
\end{aligned}
$$

so the radial source is $+\left[\rho(v_2^2 + v_3^2) + 2p\right]/r$ and the polar source is
$+\cot\theta\,(\rho v_3^2 + p)/r - \rho v_1v_2/r$. The signs match the code, which subtracts each source from the
divergence (`div[IVX] -= src1`) before the update $\Delta\mathbf U = -\Delta t\,(\nabla\cdot\mathbf F)$
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}).

To average a source over the cell, the code assumes that each factor of the geometry averages on its own.
The measure separates as $r^2\,\mathrm{d}r$ times $\sin\theta\,\mathrm{d}\theta$, so the factor $1/r$ is replaced by
its volume average and the factor $\cot\theta$ by its own, while $\rho$[^rg-9ad8c245b530], $\mathbf v$[^rg-0384f104c8ca] and $p$[^rg-fc67e812a387] keep their cell values:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i} &= \frac{\tfrac12\left(r_+^2 - r_-^2\right)}{\tfrac13\left(r_+^3 - r_-^3\right)}, \\
\langle\cot\theta\rangle_{V_i} &= \frac{\sin\theta_+ - \sin\theta_-}{\cos\theta_- - \cos\theta_+}.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are `coord_src1_i` and `coord_src1_j` (`coord_src3_j` is the same value). Without face pressures the radial
source is, to second order,

$$
S^{(1)}_i = \langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i}\left[\rho_i\left(v_{2,i}^2 + v_{3,i}^2\right) + 2p_i\right],
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1}

computed in `forward` as `src1` ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}), which is subtracted from the divergence
row of $m_1$[^rg-a998e68d3e21]. The approximation is the replacement of the cell average of a product by the product of cell values,
an error of $O(\Delta x_a^2)$ in each direction $a$.

When the Riemann solver returns the face pressures $p_{i\pm1/2}$ and they are inside the $m_1$ flux, the code
replaces $2p_i\langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i}$ by

$$
S^{p}_i = \frac{A_{i+1/2}\,p_{i+1/2} - A_{i-1/2}\,p_{i-1/2}}{V_i} - \frac{p_{i+1/2} - p_{i-1/2}}{\Delta x_{1,i}}.
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-facep}

@eq-ch03-sphpolar-facep is the `pressure_gradient` branch ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}). Its
first term cancels the pressure part of the flux divergence exactly, so the net pressure force on $m_1$ is
$-(p_{i+1/2} - p_{i-1/2})/\Delta x_{1,i}$, the plain face difference. For a uniform $p$ it equals $p\,(A_{i+1/2} -
A_{i-1/2})/V_i = 2p\,\langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i}$ by @eq-ch03-sphpolar-metric, so it agrees with
@eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1 in that limit. Under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` the face difference is replaced by `x1_pressure_source`,
the $r^2$-weighted moment of a quintic through six faces ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}); @sec-ch05 derives it.

For $m_2$ the polar source derived above has two parts. The curvature part
$\langle r^{-1}\rangle\langle\cot\theta\rangle(\rho v_3^2 + p)$ is applied as written
(`div[IVY] -= coord_src1_i * coord_src1_j * m_pp`). The part $-\rho v_1v_2/r = -T_{r\theta}/r$ the code puts in
angular-momentum form: moved back to the left side as $+T_{r\theta}/r$, it joins the radial flux term through
$\frac{1}{r^2}\partial_r\left(r^2T_{r\theta}\right) + \frac{T_{r\theta}}{r} = \frac{1}{r^3}\partial_r\left(r^3T_{r\theta}\right)$,
the divergence of the flux of $r\,m_2$. Combined with the $x_1$ flux
divergence of $m_2$, the target form is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\frac{A_{i+1/2}f^{(2)}_{i+1/2} - A_{i-1/2}f^{(2)}_{i-1/2}}{V_i}
+ c_i\left(A_{i-1/2}f^{(2)}_{i-1/2} + A_{i+1/2}f^{(2)}_{i+1/2}\right) \\
&\qquad = \frac{r_+A_{i+1/2}f^{(2)}_{i+1/2} - r_-A_{i-1/2}f^{(2)}_{i-1/2}}{x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}\,V_i},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-sphpolar-angmom}

with $c_i = \Delta x_{1,i}/[(r_- + r_+)V_i]$. Writing $A_\pm = A_{i\pm1/2}$ and $f_\pm = f^{(2)}_{i\pm1/2}$, the identity
takes three lines:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{A_+f_+ - A_-f_-}{V_i} + c_i\left(A_-f_- + A_+f_+\right)
&= \frac{A_+f_+\left(1 + \frac{\Delta x_{1,i}}{r_- + r_+}\right) - A_-f_-\left(1 - \frac{\Delta x_{1,i}}{r_- + r_+}\right)}{V_i} \\
&= \frac{2\left(r_+A_+f_+ - r_-A_-f_-\right)}{(r_- + r_+)V_i} \\
&= \frac{r_+A_+f_+ - r_-A_-f_-}{x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}V_i}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The second line uses $1 \pm \Delta x_{1,i}/(r_- + r_+) = 2r_\pm/(r_- + r_+)$, since $\Delta x_{1,i} = r_+ - r_-$;
the third uses $r_- + r_+ = 2x^{\mathrm m}_{1,i}$. The right side
is a difference of face quantities divided by $x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}V_i$, so $\sum_i x^{\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}V_i m_{2,i}$
changes only through the domain-end faces: the $x_1$ fluxes conserve this discrete angular momentum. The same form is
used for $m_3$, and for $m_3$ along $x_2$ with $\sin\theta$ in place of $r$. The code coefficient is `coord_src2_i`
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::reset >}}), and the term is added to the $m_2$ and $m_3$ rows through `face_area1`
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}); the Limits layer records how the code's area factor
differs from @eq-ch03-sphpolar-angmom.

What is exact: the measures, the centroids, the coefficient averages and the telescoping identity. What is truncated:
the product averages in @eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1, at $O(\Delta x_a^2)$ in each direction $a$. The tests cited below check the measures, the centroids, the
coefficients and the face-pressure form in the code.

::: {.callout-important title="Check"}
The coefficient averages, the centroid and the two source identities are checked exactly in sympy (`[C4]`,
`[C5]`).[^sph-c]
:::

[^sph-c]: `python3 src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch03/checks/geometry_check.out`,
    lines `[C4]` and `[C5]`; a sympy restatement of `SphericalPolarImpl::reset` and `SphericalPolarImpl::forward` at
    the pin, CPU, double; Python 3.11.13, numpy 2.4.6, sympy 1.14.0.

### Numerical method

`x1v` and `x2v` hold the centroids of @eq-ch03-sphpolar-centroids, `x3v` the midpoint; the widths `dx1f`, `dx2f`,
`dx3f` are face differences of the sliced faces, ghosts included, and `dx1v`, `dx2v`, `dx3v` centroid spacings. On a
stretched $x_1$ declared by `geometry/x1f` or `geometry/cells/x1rat` (@sec-ch03-globalgrid) the radial faces are the
deck's, with ghost widths mirrored at each end, and every formula above takes them as they are; the coordinate
accepts a stretched $x_1$ only when the declared $x_2$ bounds exclude both poles, $0<x_2^{\min}$ and
$x_2^{\max}<\pi$ ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::CoordinateImpl >}}). The
transverse lengths used by diffusion and the curl, `center_width2` $= r\,\Delta\theta$ and `center_width3`
$= r\sin\theta\,\Delta\varphi$, are taken at the centroids. All are built once in `reset`; a mesh generator triggers a
rebuild from the moved faces. The sources run in every stage, in `forward`, after the flux divergence and before the
stage update, and only on interior cells for the face-flux terms; the point-value terms use the primitives of the
whole block. @fig-ch03-sphpolar-centroids shows where the three radial positions of a cell lie.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-sphpolar-centroids
#| fig-cap: "A spherical-polar shell cell between $r_-$ and $r_+$ with its midpoint $x^{\\mathrm{m}}_{1,i}$, its volume centroid $x_{1,i}$ (where the cell value is stored) and the face-measure centroid of its $x_2$ and $x_3$ faces. The arrow marks the outward radial source."
#| fig-alt: "A wedge-shaped shell cell with three radial tick marks, for the midpoint, the volume centroid and the face centroid."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.figures.fig_sphpolar_centroids import make_fig
make_fig()
```

With one $x_2$ cell (`nx2` = 1) there is no $x_2$ flux; the $m_3$ source then uses the point form
$\langle r^{-1}\rangle\langle\cot\theta\rangle\rho v_3v_2$ instead of the $x_2$ angular-momentum form. The
shallow-water equation of state drops the pressure terms from the $m_1$ and $m_2$ sources. The face pressures
`_face_pressure1` exist whenever a block has more than one $x_1$ cell ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::reset >}}), so in a hydro
run the face-pressure form @eq-ch03-sphpolar-facep is the one that runs and @eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1 keeps its
pressure term only on blocks with a single $x_1$ cell.

: Code map of the spherical-polar metric. {#tbl-ch03-sphpolar-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-sphpolar-code):

1. `reset` refuses an $x_2$ range outside $[0,\pi]$ with "Spherical-polar coordinates require x2 in [0, pi]" when
   there is more than one $x_2$ cell ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::reset >}}).
2. It zeroes the cosine buffers and builds the widths and, with `radial_centers`, the centroids
   ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::reset >}}), then the five coefficients `coord_src1_i` to `coord_src3_j`
   ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::reset >}}).
3. In each stage `forward` calls the base divergence, then forms `src1` with one of three pressure forms: the quintic
   moment when `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` is set and its stencil is usable, the face-pressure form when face pressures
   are given, else $2p\langle r^{-1}\rangle$ ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}).
4. It adds the $m_2$ curvature term and the $x_1$ angular-momentum terms of $m_2$ and $m_3$, then the $x_2$
   angular-momentum term of $m_3$ or, with one $x_2$ cell, its point form, as `use_x2_fluxes` selects
   ({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}).

**How to use it — construction card.** A spherical-polar shell between two radii, with the colatitude given
in units of $\pi$. Replace `geometry` in a copy of `straka_single.yaml` saved as `deck.yaml` with the following. This card is
not runnable with the `straka` driver: its initial state treats $x_1$ as height, not radius.

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `x2max_pi`[^rg-f2733a81186c].
```yaml
geometry:
  type: spherical-polar
  bounds: {x1min: 6.4e6, x1max: 6.5e6, x2min_pi: 0.25, x2max_pi: 0.75, x3min: 0., x3max: 0.1}   # r [m], theta, phi [rad]
  cells: {nx1: 8, nx2: 8, nx3: 1, nghost: 2}
```

With the source-built Python interface, construct the mesh without initializing or advancing the Straka state:

```bash
python -c 'import snapy; mesh = snapy.Mesh(snapy.MeshOptions.from_yaml("deck.yaml")); print(len(mesh.blocks))'
```

This builds **1 block**.

Refused: with more than one $x_2$ cell, an $x_2$ range outside $[0,\pi]$ stops `reset` with "Spherical-polar
coordinates require x2 in [0, pi], got [-0.1, 1]"; with `nx2: 1` the same range is accepted. The face-pressure form
@eq-ch03-sphpolar-facep needs no key: it runs whenever the block has more than one $x_1$ cell. The check and the
coefficients $\langle r^{-1}\rangle_{V_i}$ and $\langle\cot\theta\rangle$ of @eq-ch03-sphpolar-src1 and the
angular-momentum coefficient $c_i$ of @eq-ch03-sphpolar-angmom are
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::reset >}}):

```cpp
  TORCH_CHECK(op->nx2() <= 1 || (op->x2min() >= 0.0 && op->x2max() <= M_PI),
              "Spherical-polar coordinates require x2 in [0, pi], got [",
              op->x2min(), ", ", op->x2max(), "]");
    ...
  auto radial_volume = (rp.pow(3) - rm.pow(3)) / 3.0;
  auto radial_area23 = 0.5 * (rp.pow(2) - rm.pow(2));
    ...
  auto polar_volume = torch::abs(theta_m.cos() - theta_p.cos());

  coord_src1_i = register_buffer(
      "coord_src1_i",
      (radial_area23 / radial_volume).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0));
  coord_src2_i = register_buffer(
      "coord_src2_i",
      (dx1f / ((rm + rp) * radial_volume)).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0));
  coord_src1_j = register_buffer(
      "coord_src1_j",
      ((sin_p - sin_m) / polar_volume).unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(-1));
```

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_coordinate` | centroids, areas, volume and the five coefficients equal reference formulas | $10^{-12}$ rel. and abs. | round-off of the closed forms |
| `test_coordinate` | with face pressures the $m_1$ row ignores the cell pressure | $10^{-6}$ rel. and abs. | set in the test |
| `test_coordinate` | the $m_1$ row is the plain face-pressure difference | $10^{-6}$ rel. and abs. | set in the test |
| `test_x1_centroid_rest_python` | a column at rest stays at rest under `SNAP_X1_CENTROID_EXACT` | `TOL_ON` $10^{-10}$ | @sec-ch05 |

: Tests of the spherical-polar metric. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-sphpolar-tests}

The reference-formula case is `geometry_matches_athena_reference_formulas`
({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp SphericalPolar.geometry_matches_athena_reference_formulas >}}); it compares `x1v`, `x2v`, the three areas, the volume and `coord_src1_i` to
`coord_src3_j` with `torch::allclose`. The face-pressure cases are
`spherical_polar_radial_source_preserves_face_pressure_gradient` and
`spherical_polar_radial_source_uses_face_pressure_in_x1_momentum` ({{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp DeviceTest.spherical_polar_radial_source_uses_face_pressure_in_x1_momentum >}}, {{< code tests/test_coordinate.cpp DeviceTest.spherical_polar_radial_source_preserves_face_pressure_gradient >}}); the first
sets the face pressure to the face radius and checks that the $m_1$ row equals
$(p_{i+1/2}-p_{i-1/2})/\Delta x_{1,i}$, the second checks that two cell pressures give the same $m_1$ row once face pressures
are given. The face-pressure cases run on CPU and, through the `DeviceTest` parameter, on CUDA when it is built; the
reference-formula case runs on CPU only. All are one block, one rank. No case checks the $m_2$ and $m_3$ source
terms. They were not run for this chapter at the pin (missing evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The $m_2$ and $m_3$ angular-momentum terms are untested: no test at the pin checks them (read from the tests).
- `nx2` = 1 uses a midpoint for `x2v`, not the polar centroid.
- A stretched $x_1$ is refused on a grid whose $x_2$ bounds reach a pole; `test_stretched_x1_ref.release`
  (`refuses_spherical_polar`, `refuses_the_off_pole_block_of_a_pole_deck`) passes at the pin on CPU (@sec-ch03-globalgrid).
:::

A hypothesis from reading the code, not measured: the angular-momentum terms of `forward` multiply `coord_src2_i`,
which divides by the radial factor $V^{(1)}_i$[^rg-bbe09e4ed06f] only, by the full face area `face_area1` $= r_\pm^2\varpi_{jk}$
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}). @eq-ch03-sphpolar-angmom needs $r_\pm^2$ there, so as
written the term carries an extra factor of the cell's solid angle $\varpi_{jk}$[^rg-3c62fd4496b8]. The $x_2$ term multiplies
`coord_src1_i` and `coord_src2_j` by the full `face_area2` $= \tfrac12(r_+^2-r_-^2)\lvert\sin\theta_\pm\rvert
\Delta\varphi$ where the $\sin\theta$ form needs $\lvert\sin\theta_\pm\rvert$ alone
({{< code src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp SphericalPolarImpl::forward >}}). If this reading is right, the $-\rho v_1v_2/r$ and
$-\rho v_1v_3/r$ terms are scaled by $\varpi_{jk}$ and the $x_2$ term by a dimensional factor, in every
multidimensional spherical-polar run with tangential velocity; a radial column with $v_2 = v_3 = 0$ does not see it.
`CoordinateImpl::forward` is not bound in Python, so the Python coordinate interface cannot measure this source term directly ({{< code python/csrc/pycoord.cpp bind_coord >}}).
A failing regression test is still needed to establish this behavior.

The `x2` refusal is skipped when there is one $x_2$ cell. The switch combinations that are tested are listed in the
switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-8f3539a20049]: $r$ — $x_1$ on a spherical-polar grid (radius) [m]

[^rg-f8c6079838f7]: $\theta$ — $x_2$ on a spherical-polar grid (colatitude) [rad]

[^rg-d44d77aee75f]: $\varphi$ — $x_3$ on a spherical-polar grid (azimuth) [rad]; never the potential

[^rg-9ad8c245b530]: $\rho$ — total density, dry plus every species that carries mass [kg m$^{-3}$]

[^rg-0384f104c8ca]: $\mathbf v = (v_1,v_2,v_3)$ — velocity [m s$^{-1}$]

[^rg-fc67e812a387]: $p$ — pressure [Pa]

[^rg-a998e68d3e21]: $m_1, m_2, m_3$ — momentum density $\rho v_a$

[^rg-f2733a81186c]: x2max_pi — upper bound of the second coordinate in multiples of pi

[^rg-bbe09e4ed06f]: $V^{(1)}_i$ — the $x_1$ factor of the cell volume, $V_{ijk}=\varpi_{jk}V^{(1)}_i$: $\tfrac13(x_{1,i+1/2}^3-x_{1,i-1/2}^3)$ on spherical-polar, $h_i$ on Cartesian; the radial factor of `cell_volume`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L200-L211)

[^rg-3c62fd4496b8]: $\varpi_{jk}$ — horizontal factor of a cell volume, $V_{ijk}=\varpi_{jk}V^{(1)}_i$: the solid angle on spherical-polar ($V^{(1)}_i=\tfrac13(r_{+}^3-r_{-}^3)$), $\Delta x_2\Delta x_3$ on Cartesian ($V^{(1)}_i=h_i$); the angular factors of `cell_volume`; [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/919936da07d80a310b98ab11da184972a3203274/src/coord/spherical_polar.cpp#L200-L211)
